senses.en: make sb. feel better when they are feeling sad or disappointed
examples: He [[consoled]] himself that he would see Kate again soon.

senses.zh: （在精神或感情上）（使）复原；（使）坚强起来
senses.en: become mentally or emotionally strong again after a bad experience, or help sb. to do this
examples: Bianca was the kind of woman who could [[heal]] his soul, if he had time to let her.
It took a long time for the wounds to [[heal]].

senses.en: (also heal up) become healthy again; make sth. healthy again
examples: Bianca was the kind of woman who could [[heal]] his soul, if he had time to let her.
It took a long time for the wounds to [[heal]].

senses.en: when two things happen at the same time, in the same place, or to the same people in a way that seems surprising or unusual
examples: I think it is more than [[coincidence]] that all the complaints have come from the same group of people.

senses.en: a treatment that helps sb. feel better, grow stronger, etc., esp. after an illness
examples: Many patients receiving these new [[therapies]] respond rapidly to them and get a lot of clinical benefit.

senses.en: (fml.) suggest sth. as a plan or course of action
examples: In his speech he [[proposed]] that the UN should set up an emergency center for the environment.

senses.en: (usu. before noun) lasting for only a short time
examples: For one [[fleeting]] moment, Paula allowed herself to forget her troubles.

senses.en: the act of betraying sb. / sth. or the fact of being betrayed
examples: She wondered if he felt hurt at his best friend's [[betrayal]] but didn't have the courage to ask.

senses.en: when you are with sb. you enjoy being with, and are not alone
examples: That feeling of [[companionship]] can make a huge difference, especially at a stressful job.

senses.zh: （尤指对复杂情况、看法的）顿悟，猛醒
senses.en: a sudden clear understanding of sth. or part of sth., esp. a complicated situation or idea
examples: The article gives us a real [[insight]] into the causes of the present economic crisis.

senses.en: (AmE also monolog) a long speech by one person
examples: Blogs are not just about one person sharing in a [[monologue]] with everyone else listening.

senses.en: in a way that is surprising because it is the opposite of what you would expect
examples: [[Paradoxically]], the economy is improving although many families complain about the poverty in which they live.

senses.en: (only before noun) belonging to mental or spiritual life
examples: [[Interior]] monolog is defined as the thoughts you have running through your brain or the things that you silently tell yourself.
The [[interior]] of the church was dark.

senses.en: the inner part or inside of sth.
examples: [[Interior]] monolog is defined as the thoughts you have running through your brain or the things that you silently tell yourself.
The [[interior]] of the church was dark.

senses.en: existing everywhere or involving everyone
examples: Smiling is apparently a [[universal]] sign of friendliness and approval.

senses.en: the quality or state of being universal
examples: His lyrics aim for a certain timeless [[universality]].

senses.en: the quality of not changing as the years go past, or as fashion changes
examples: It is said that all diamonds are symbolic of love, commitment, and [[timelessness]], but adding yellow to the stone gives it even deeper meaning.

senses.en: existing in the mind but not immediately available to consciousness
examples: There are conscious thoughts that you're aware of and [[subconscious]] ones that you're not.

senses.en: make or become less severe, difficult, unpleasant, painful, etc.
examples: The school needs to take some measures to [[ease]] the burden on busy teachers.
He studied hard every day so that he could pass the exam with [[ease]].

senses.en: the fact that sth. is easy to do
examples: The school needs to take some measures to [[ease]] the burden on busy teachers.
He studied hard every day so that he could pass the exam with [[ease]].

senses.en: (also empathic) having the ability to understand sb. else's feelings or emotions
examples: Providing a loving home environment can help the child to become independent, self-confident, and [[empathetic]] toward others.

senses.en: a mild illness or health problem is not serious
examples: She had a [[mild]] headache, and went to bed much earlier than usual.
I like this kind of cheese because it has a pleasant [[mild]] flavor.

senses.en: not very strong or hot-tasting
examples: She had a [[mild]] headache, and went to bed much earlier than usual.
I like this kind of cheese because it has a pleasant [[mild]] flavor.

senses.en: sth. wrong with your body or mind which shows that you have a particular illness
examples: Tiredness is one of the most common [[symptoms]] of stress.

senses.en: in a way that happens repeatedly
examples: We are [[continually]] reassessing the situation.
The telephone has been ringing [[continually]] in the office all morning.

senses.en: in a way that continues for a long time without stopping
examples: We are [[continually]] reassessing the situation.
The telephone has been ringing [[continually]] in the office all morning.

senses.zh: （尤指因所爱之人去世而）感到悲痛
senses.en: feel extremely sad, esp. because sb. you love has died
examples: He died, and every day since then I have [[grieved]] for him.

senses.en: the events that form the main story of a book, film, or play
examples: Although the cast (全体演员) was different back then, the [[plot]] was strikingly similar.

senses.zh: 虚构的；编造的；小说（中）的
senses.en: fictional people, events, etc. are imaginary and from a book or story
examples: He has created many lively [[fictional]] characters with his wonderful writing.

senses.en: when you stop working, usu. because of your age
examples: He became a keen golfer after his [[retirement]] from politics.

senses.zh: 短暂的；转瞬即逝的；一时的
senses.en: (fml.) continuing only for a short time
examples: The trading data show that these events had minimal and [[transient]] effect on the price of gold and silver.

senses.en: the state of continuing only for a short time
examples: History is a combination of permanence and [[transience]].

senses.en: (of a situation) complicated and unpleasant to deal with
examples: If you find yourself in a [[messy]] situation, please take these five strategies to heart.
Sorry, the place is so [[messy]] because I haven't had time to clear up.

senses.en: dirty or untidy
examples: If you find yourself in a [[messy]] situation, please take these five strategies to heart.
Sorry, the place is so [[messy]] because I haven't had time to clear up.

senses.zh: 悲痛，极度悲伤（尤指因所爱之人去世）
senses.en: extreme sadness, esp. because sb. you love has died
examples: The [[grief]] she felt over Helen's death was almost unbearable.

senses.en: a feeling that you have no hope at all
examples: A few positive words can turn [[despair]] into hope.

senses.en: (fml.) a short piece of writing about a person or place that you knew well, or an event that you experienced
examples: Her [[memoir]] of her friend will be published soon.
Angelou's first volume of [[memoirs]] dealt with her childhood.

senses.en: (~s) a book by sb. important and famous in which they write about their life and experiences
examples: Her [[memoir]] of her friend will be published soon.
Angelou's first volume of [[memoirs]] dealt with her childhood.

senses.en: (fml.) the act, process, or skill of telling a story
examples: The novel contains too much dialog and not enough [[narrative]].
At several points in the [[narrative]] the two stories cross.

senses.en: (fml.) a description of events in a story, esp. in a novel
examples: The novel contains too much dialog and not enough [[narrative]].
At several points in the [[narrative]] the two stories cross.

senses.en: believing that good things will happen in the future
examples: Bankers are cautiously [[optimistic]] about the country's economic future.

senses.zh: 一个接一个地；接二连三地
senses.en: (also one after another) if a series of events or actions happen one after the other, each one happens soon after the previous one
examples: The children walked silently, [[one after the other]], into the schoolhouse to begin their lesson.

senses.en: because you want sth. to happen
examples: Shoppers flocked to the sales in the hope of finding a bargain.

senses.zh: 米歇尔・德・蒙田 ( 法国作家、哲学家 )
萨塞克斯大学 (英国大学，位于英格兰)
海伦・加纳 （澳大利亚作家）
